info.title: Farmer API
info.description:
The REST API that the `farmer` CLI uses. Every call acts as one person and can do only what that person can do in the web app.

## Authentication

Send a token in the `Authorization` header:

```sh
curl "$FARMER/api/v1/me" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
```

The examples set `FARMER` to your deployment's address. There are two kinds of token.

### API token (recommended)

Use an API token for a script, a scheduled job or an integration. Make one in Farmer at [Preferences → API tokens](/:org/settings/preferences#api-tokens). A token starts with `fmr_`, and Farmer shows it only once.

- **Access.** A read-only token gets 403 `forbidden` on a request that changes data. Give the token write access only if the script needs it.
- **Workspaces.** A token can work in one workspace only, or in all the workspaces of its owner.
- **Expiry.** A token expires after 30 days, 90 days or one year, or never. Revoke a token [in Preferences](/:org/settings/preferences#api-tokens) at any time.

### Device flow

The `farmer` CLI uses the device flow ([RFC 8628](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8628)), because a person approves each login in a browser. Use it for a tool that a person runs interactively. Do not use it for a script that runs without a person.

**1. Ask for a code.**

```sh
curl -X POST "$FARMER/api/auth/device/code" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"client_id": "farmer-cli"}'
```

The answer holds `device_code`, `verification_uri_complete` and `interval`.

**2. Approve it.** Open `verification_uri_complete` in a browser, sign in and approve the code.

**3. Collect the token.** Send this every `interval` seconds until the answer holds `access_token`:

```sh
curl -X POST "$FARMER/api/auth/device/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "grant_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code",
    "device_code": "<device_code>",
    "client_id": "farmer-cli"
  }'
```

**4. Use it** as the bearer token.

`DELETE /session` revokes the token that the request sends, of either kind.

## Organizations

Most routes start with `/orgs/{orgSlug}`. `GET /me` lists the slugs the token can use. A token for one workspace lists only that workspace.

## Errors

An error answers the `Error` body. Branch on `code`, not on the `error` text.

| Status | `code` | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | No token, a token that is not valid or has expired, or an organization the person is not in or the token cannot use. |
| 403 | `forbidden` | The person may not do this, for example log time on a project they are not assigned to. A read-only API token also gets 403 on a request that changes data. |
| 404 | `not_found` | No such record. |
| 422 | `invalid_input` | The body or the query is not valid, or the values break a rule, such as a day over 24 hours. `issues` names each field. |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | Too many calls. Wait for `Retry-After` seconds. |
| 500 | `server_error` | Something failed on the server. |

The CLI also sends `x-farmer-cli-version` and can get 426 `cli_outdated`. Other clients do not send the header, so they never get 426.

## Compatibility

A response can get new fields at any time. Ignore the fields you do not know.

bearer.description: An API token from [Preferences → API tokens](/:org/settings/preferences#api-tokens) (recommended), or the `access_token` from the device flow.

error.description: A sentence for a person. Its wording can change at any time.

code.description: What a client branches on. A new code is an addition.

issues.description: One item per invalid field, on `invalid_input`.

Error.description: The body of every error response.

cliEnabled.description: False when this deployment has the API switched off. Every other route then answers 404.

organizations.description: Each slug is the `orgSlug` of every other route.

anyOf.description: The role the caller holds on the project.

fillsDay.description: A rest-of-day block: its duration follows the day, nobody typed it.

synced.description: Mirrors a calendar event. Google still owns it unless it was filed.

project.description: Null for time off, a Break, and anything not yet filed.

blockedDays.description: The days a week copy left alone because they would pass 24 hours. Always empty for a day copy.

skipped.description: A weekend, a public holiday or a day already off.

anyOf.description: The role the caller holds on the project.

tasks.description: Work tasks, to log time against.

status.description: Null when no target applies to the person.

stillRunning.description: The sync took longer than the request may stay open and continues on the server. The four lists are then empty.

droppedAt.description: Set when the timer passed the person's limit and was dropped. Nothing was logged. Null while it runs.

snappedSeconds.description: What confirming would log: the elapsed time, snapped to the nearest quarter hour.

serverNow.description: The instant `elapsedSeconds` was measured at. Count from this, not from the local clock.

entry.description: The entry this timer continues, or null when confirming logs a new one.

organization.description: A timer belongs to the person, not to an organization, so another organization can answer it. `here` says whether it runs in this one.

TimeEntryPatch.description: Any subset of the entry's fields. Each one replaces the stored value; `null` clears an optional field.
